external_contracts: ssl3_write_bytes: live connection s; write BIO owned by the caller; buf readable for len bytes, never dereferenced when len == 0. Returns 1 on success (the caller sets *written), -1 on a record/BIOS failure.

ssl3_read_bytes / ssl3_read_one_record: live connection; read BIO owned by the caller; buf writable for cap bytes; rectype writable. A record whose plaintext exceeds cap is consumed and dropped with -1 (B25-R3).

tls13_next_handshake_message: live connection; buf writable for cap bytes; the buffered state (rd_msg_len/off) is private to this module and satisfies rd_msg_off <= rd_msg_len <= rd_msg_buf.len() at every use.

BIO callbacks are application-controlled reentrancy edges. No Rust reference or non-reentrant borrow is held across BIO_read/BIO_write/BIO_ctrl; a callback must not free or re-enter the same connection (B25-R1).

The record accumulator fields (rec_hdr_len, rec_body_len, rd_msg_len, rd_msg_off) are zero-initialised by the zero-valid Ssl constructor and written only by this module; any future writer must preserve the bounds above (B25-R5).

boundaries.mechanism: record write path: ssl3_write_bytes fragmentation, ssl3_write_one_record encode/header, ssl3_write_all BIO transport and flush
boundaries.contract: ssl3_write_bytes fragments at SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH; a zero-length request returns success without writing (authority tot == len). ssl3_write_one_record refuses len > SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH, so the 17000-byte encoder scratch and the two-byte length field are always in range. ssl3_write_all advances only while off < len and surfaces a retryable BIO failure as -1 with rwstate = SSL_WRITING.

boundaries.mechanism: record read accumulator and resumption: ssl3_read_one_record (header/body), over-long record arm, ssl3_read_bytes_rlayer_return EOF/retry classification
boundaries.contract: The five-byte header and the declared body are accumulated in rec_hdr/rec_body with off < bound at every add; the declared length is bounded by rec_body.len() before the body loop; cap is checked before every caller-buffer copy; a short BIO_read resumes from the retained field state. The over-long header is fatal (record overflow) because the header bytes are already consumed.

boundaries.mechanism: TLS1.3 handshake-message buffering: tls13_next_handshake_message multi-message drain and non-handshake record skip
boundaries.contract: A buffered message is delivered only when p + 4 <= rd_msg_len (so the four header bytes are initialised) and p + msg_len <= rd_msg_len && msg_len <= cap; otherwise nothing is copied. A fully consumed non-handshake record is discarded and now clears rd_msg_len/rd_msg_off before returning -1, so its body cannot be reparsed as a handshake header.

Only exactly two alert bytes are read (len != 2 is fatal before any byte access); the caller's buffer is writable for the record body, which ssl3_read_one_record bounds by cap. The warning/fatal/close_notify classification and the ERR coordinate match rec_layer_s3.c:864-944; raise_alert_received uses static strings and a NUL-terminated heap message the error setter copies.

boundaries.mechanism: record-layer state accessors: RECORD_LAYER_write_pending/read_pending, SSL_CTX_set_default_read_buffer_len, SSL_set_default_read_buffer_len, SSL_rstate_string(_long)
boundaries.contract: All entry points take NULL-or-live pointers, test NULL before any dereference, and return either a scalar field, 0, or a pointer to a process-lifetime C string literal. The context setter's NULL arm is a documented safety improvement (the authority dereferences NULL); the connection setter's NULL arm matches. No allocation, reference or lifetime is created.

Decrypts into the full-size rx_buf (TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN = 16384) and copies min(num, n) to the caller, so no record is dropped for a small application buffer; the returned n is bounded by the cap.

Two-byte stack array, readable for len 2; the write path bounds the record.
Two-byte alert array; wbio is NULL-checked before the call and BIO_write(NULL) is a safe refusal.
16384-byte stack buffers matching the buffer's cap; results are read only when n > 0.

residuals.description: BIO_read/BIO_write/BIO_ctrl invoke application-controlled callbacks. No Rust reference or borrow is held across them (all connection access is through raw pointers), but a callback that frees or re-enters the same connection can invalidate s or interleave the record accumulator. This is the authority's non-reentrant record-layer contract and is not enforceable in this file.

A retryable or zero BIO_write after the record header has been committed leaves a partial record in the transport; the pending-write resumption (wpend_tot/re-entry) is not modelled, so a retry starts a new record. The function doc states this. It is a stream-integrity residual, not UB, and the authority's own failure handling is likewise not rolled back at this layer.

A record whose plaintext exceeds the caller's cap is fully consumed from the BIO and dropped with -1. The authority retains the record and copies at most the caller's length. Only the 2048-byte SSL_shutdown discard and the 16-byte TLS1.2 CCS reader can hit this; neither loses protocol-relevant data. Not UB.

A zero-length record returns 0 from ssl3_read_bytes, so SSL_read's callers treat it as terminal, where the authority's `totalbytes == 0 -> goto start` skips empty records and keeps reading. The reduced reader does not distinguish an empty completed record from the EOF/retry return. Not UB; no test currently drives an empty record.

rec_hdr_len <= 5, rec_body_len <= declared length, rd_msg_len <= rd_msg_buf.len() and rd_msg_off <= rd_msg_len are established by SSL_new's zero initialisation and by this module's writes. The fields are pub within the crate; any future writer must preserve them. The buffered-message accesses are array-bounds checked and the copies are additionally guarded.
